title: Backend + Database
goal: Build a REST API backed by Postgres from a client brief, with validation and tests. This is the start of the booking product.
outcomes: Write typed, tested TypeScript with an AI agent you control through a rules file
Design REST endpoints with correct verbs, status codes and a consistent error format
Model a booking domain in Postgres with constraints that make invalid states impossible
Prevent double bookings with a partial unique index and a locking transaction
Validate input with Zod and prove behaviour with Vitest + Supertest
Review AI-written code and tests critically
projectStage: Booking API v1 — architecture: Express routes → services → data access (Drizzle) → Postgres (pgvector image). Starts from a messy WhatsApp message from a salon owner.

days.title: AI Dev Setup, TypeScript + Git Workflow
learn: Node.js, npm, package.json scripts, TypeScript basics (types, interfaces, unions), folder structure, ESLint + Prettier, Vitest basics

Modern JavaScript: arrow functions, template strings, destructuring, spread/rest, optional chaining, nullish coalescing, ES modules, map/filter/reduce/find/some/every/sort, immutability, callbacks, closures, the event loop
AI + Git workflow: project rules file (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md), scoped requests, reading a diff before accepting it, branches, pull requests, merge conflicts
tasks: Install anything skipped in Week 0 (Node.js LTS, VS Code, a chat tutor), plus Docker Desktop and two of Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. Run docker run hello-world.
Create a TypeScript project with lint, format and dev scripts.

Write pure functions for a contact list: case-insensitive search by partial name, count by first letter (reduce), sort by name without mutating the original array, and updateContact(contact, changes) that returns a new object using spread. Check them with a few Vitest tests. Do this on a feature branch, open a PR and review the diff.
Write a rules file for the AI agent (stack, folder structure, "never commit secrets", "run tests before saying done").
Ask the AI agent to explain one file in plain words, then check the explanation against the code and note what it got wrong.
Give the same scoped request to two of Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, and compare the diffs.
acceptance: npm install && npm run dev works from a clean clone.
Lint passes with zero errors.
Original arrays and objects are never mutated (tested).
Commits are small, with clear one-line messages.
PR merged with a description and a "How I verified this" section.

days.title: HTTP Server + REST
learn: API styles (REST, webhooks, WebSockets) and when each fits
Vite as a frontend dev server, AbortController
HTTP verbs, status codes, headers, Content-Type
Express setup, nodemon or Node's watch mode, express.Router, middleware order, JSON body parsing, 404 handler, error handler, .env config
tasks: Create /ping returning { "msg": "pong" } and /health returning uptime and timestamp.
Build CRUD for /services (name, duration, price) using an in-memory array.
Test every route with Bruno and commit the collection to the repo (Postman works too; curl for quick checks).

On a feature branch, port the Week 0 weather widget (or test-out page) into a Vite + TypeScript project and run it with npm run dev. Add AbortController so a new city search cancels the previous requests. Open a PR and review the diff.
Create and resolve one merge conflict on purpose.
acceptance: Port comes from .env. .env is gitignored and .env.example is committed.
Every route returns the right status code (200, 201, 204, 400, 404), with a JSON body on every non-204 response.
Invalid JSON returns 400 with a clear message, not a crash.
An unknown path returns a 404 JSON error, not Express's default HTML page.
The merge conflict and how it was resolved are explained in the PR.
The Bruno collection passes with bru run.
The Vite port builds with npm run build and zero type errors. Searching again before a result arrives never shows the older result.

days.title: Postgres + SQL by Hand
learn: Run Postgres with docker compose (pgvector/pgvector:pg17 image so Week 5 works without changes); connect with psql and a GUI
Tables, data types, primary keys, foreign keys, ON DELETE CASCADE vs RESTRICT, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, defaults, timestamptz
SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT/OFFSET, RETURNING, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (upsert)
INNER and LEFT JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING, indexes
tasks: Design customers, services, staff, staff_hours (weekday, opens_at, closes_at) and bookings tables.
Make customers.email UNIQUE.
Write 10 queries by hand: bookings for a day, bookings per customer, customers with zero bookings, revenue per service, and so on.
Add a partial unique index that blocks two active bookings for the same staff member at the same start time: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON bookings (staff_id, starts_at) WHERE status <> 'cancelled'.
Add an index on bookings.starts_at and explain why.
Choose ON DELETE CASCADE or RESTRICT for each foreign key and justify it in one line.
acceptance: Duplicate email insert fails with a constraint error.
Double booking fails at the database level, and a cancelled slot can be booked again.
Deleting a parent row cascades or is blocked as chosen, shown with one query each.
Can explain INNER vs LEFT JOIN with an example from this schema.

days.title: Connect the API to the Database
learn: Drizzle ORM (and reading the SQL it generates), parameterized queries, migrations as versioned files, seed scripts
Separating routes, services and data access; connection pools; handling database errors
Transactions and row locks (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), EXPLAIN ANALYZE, pg_trgm indexes for text search
tasks: Replace the in-memory array with Postgres.
Split the API into routes, services and data access modules. Routes never touch the database directly.
Reject overlapping bookings in the service layer, inside a transaction that locks the staff row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE).
Add migrations and a seed script (seed 10,000 bookings across at least 5,000 customers so query plans are realistic).
Enable pg_trgm in a migration and add a GIN index on customer name.
Build POST /bookings and GET /bookings?date=, with pagination (LIMIT/OFFSET or cursor) and search by customer name (ILIKE).
Ask the AI agent to write inline documentation for the data layer, then fix anything that does not match the code.
Stop Postgres and observe what the API does.
acceptance: Database can be dropped and rebuilt from migrations + seed with one command.
With Postgres down, the API returns a 500 JSON response with no stack trace leaked.
Overlapping bookings (a 60-minute booking at 10:00, then one at 10:30) return 409 Conflict with a readable message.
No route handler contains SQL or ORM calls.
Pagination and search run in SQL, not by fetching everything and filtering in JavaScript.
pg_trgm is enabled in a migration, a GIN index supports name search, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows it being used for a search of 3+ characters.

days.title: Validation + Tests
learn: Zod schemas, a consistent error response format
Vitest + Supertest, test database setup, what makes a good test, how to review tests an AI wrote
tasks: Add Zod validation to every route.
Write a happy-path test and at least one failure test per route.
Ask the AI agent to write tests for one route, then review and correct them.
Break the code on purpose and confirm a test goes red.
acceptance: npm test is green.
Invalid input returns 400 with field-level errors.
The mentor breaks 3 lines of their choice, and at least one test goes red for each.

days.title: Debug Lab (no AI)
learn: VS Code debugger, breakpoints, reading stack traces
The raw pg driver (node-postgres) and its connection pool
brokenLab: A SQL query built by string concatenation (SQL injection)
A missing await that returns a Promise instead of data
A missing foreign key, so bookings point at deleted customers and the revenue report silently drops them
A pool client that is never released (the API hangs after 10 requests)
A price column stored as text, so sorting by price is wrong
A GROUP BY report that returns duplicate rows
tasks: Fix all seven bugs in the provided booking API, with a test for each fix.
acceptance: All seven fixed, with a test for each fix.
No unhandled promise rejections.
Schema fixes applied as a new migration, not by hand-editing the database.
Each fix written up as: symptom → cause → fix → how verified.

days.title: Weekly Project: Booking API v1
tasks: Starts from a client brief: a messy WhatsApp message from a salon owner about double bookings and phone cancellations.
Write a 1-page scope first: entities, endpoints, business rules, and what is out of scope.
Endpoints: services CRUD, customers CRUD, create, list (paginated and searchable) and cancel bookings, availability for a date.
Business rules: no double bookings, no bookings in the past, cancelling sets a status instead of deleting the row.
CSV import script for the client's customer list: imports the good rows, reports bad rows with line numbers, and a re-run creates no duplicates.
Migrations + seed, Zod validation, tests, Bruno collection.
acceptance: See the rubric on the Project tab.

project.name: Booking API v1
project.brief: A messy WhatsApp message from a salon owner about double bookings and phone cancellations.

Services CRUD, customers CRUD, create/list/cancel bookings, availability for a date
No double bookings, no bookings in the past, cancelling sets a status instead of deleting
CSV import: good rows imported, bad rows reported with line numbers, re-run creates no duplicates
Migrations + seed, Zod validation, tests, Bruno collection

Rebuild the availability endpoint in Python (FastAPI), Go or Ruby (Rails)
